name: Synapse Serverless SQL
oneLiner: Query files in the data lake with on-demand, pay-per-query SQL.
whatItIs: Serverless SQL is the on-demand query engine inside Azure Synapse: it runs T-SQL directly over files in ADLS (Parquet, CSV, JSON, Delta) with nothing to provision and billing only for data processed. It's the Azure equivalent of 'SQL over the lake' — the same idea as Athena on AWS. You point it at files with OPENROWSET or define external tables, and analysts query them as if they were database tables. It ships as an always-available endpoint in every Synapse workspace, so there's no cluster to start.

inPractice.narrative: Curated Parquet lands in ADLS from a Spark or pipeline job. Instead of loading it into a provisioned warehouse, analysts query it directly with serverless SQL — either ad-hoc via OPENROWSET or through external tables and views. Power BI can connect for lightweight reporting. It's the cheap, no-setup way to explore or serve lake data before (or instead of) committing to a dedicated SQL pool.

coreConcepts.detail: Query a file or folder in ADLS inline without defining a table — the fastest way to peek at lake data with SQL.
Define reusable schemas over lake files (via external data sources and file formats), then query them like normal tables; views layer logic on top.
You're billed per TB the query processes from the lake — so file format, compression and partitioning drive both speed and cost, exactly like Athena.
Every Synapse workspace has a built-in serverless SQL endpoint — no provisioning, no pausing; it's just there when you query.
Reads Parquet, CSV, JSON and Delta Lake; Parquet/Delta are far cheaper to query than raw CSV/JSON.
filepath() and filename() let queries prune to specific partitions/folders, cutting data processed.

whenToUse: Ad-hoc T-SQL exploration of files in ADLS with no infrastructure.
Lightweight serving/reporting over lake data before building a warehouse.
Cost-sensitive or spiky querying where paying per query beats a running pool.
Creating logical (external-table) views over the lake for analysts.
Quick validation of pipeline outputs sitting as Parquet in the lake.
whenNotToUse: High-concurrency, low-latency BI serving to many users — a dedicated SQL pool is faster.
Heavy repeated scans over huge unoptimised data — per-query cost mounts up.
Workloads needing indexes, updates or full warehouse features — it's read-oriented over files.
Sub-second interactive apps — there's per-query overhead.

keyFacts.label: Model
keyFacts.value: Serverless, on-demand T-SQL over ADLS files.

keyFacts.label: Billing
keyFacts.value: Per TB of data processed (with a small minimum per query).

keyFacts.label: Provisioning
keyFacts.value: None — built-in endpoint in every Synapse workspace.

keyFacts.label: Best for
keyFacts.value: Exploration and light serving, not heavy concurrent BI.

pricingShape: Billed purely on data processed per query (per TB), so there is no idle cost — no queries, no compute charge beyond the underlying ADLS storage. The entire cost lever is how much data each query reads: Parquet/Delta plus partition pruning can turn a terabyte scan into gigabytes. A careless query over raw CSV, or over an unpartitioned folder, both runs slowly and costs more. There's a minimum data-processed charge per query to be aware of for very small reads.
gotchas: Querying raw CSV/JSON is dramatically more expensive than Parquet/Delta for the same rows — convert first.
Cost is per data processed, so wide SELECT * over big folders bills for everything read.
It can't update data or enforce indexes — it's a read layer over files, not a warehouse.
Wrong ADLS permissions or credential setup causes opaque access errors in OPENROWSET/external tables.
Not sized for many concurrent low-latency queries; heavy BI belongs on a dedicated pool or Power BI import.

equivalents.name: Amazon Athena
equivalents.note: The direct analogue — serverless, pay-per-scan SQL over object-store files.

equivalents.name: BigLake
equivalents.note: Query lake files as tables; BigQuery external tables serve the same on-demand role.
